# Final audit against the authoritative rubric

Audit date: **2026-11-19**. Authority: [the student's supplied request/rubric](authoritative_audit_request.md).
The full rubric is now available and its **1,000-1,500-word report limit is settled**.
The original [report template](report_template.md) is preserved unchanged; its old
2,000-3,000 footer is superseded, not a remaining requirement conflict.

**Mandatory compliance is incomplete.** Of 39 mandatory rubric/checklist bullets
mapped individually (including repeated submission-checklist criteria), 34 are
PASS, two are PARTIAL, and three are FAIL. Eight bootstrap helpers lack docstrings;
eight confirmed bootstrap spacing errors affect both PEP 8 and lint-verification
criteria. A focused follow-up additionally confirmed a startup-interrupt exit-status
defect (F3). These findings await review; no Python/test source was changed.
Final report wording and the agreed physical Ctrl+C result remain user readiness
gates; neither approval nor a manual observation has been invented.

### CQ4: confirmed mandatory gap, reproduction and smallest correction

tests/cli_helpers.py::_BOOTSTRAP defines 14 functions executed in subprocesses.
Eight lack docstrings: controlled_input (line 30), fail_history (42), fail_read
(48), denied_read (54), denied_identity (62), denied_home (66),
interrupted_export (72), interrupted_summary (76).

Reproduce with the standard-library AST: parse tests/cli_helpers.py, literal_eval
the _BOOTSTRAP assignment, parse that returned script, and select FunctionDef
nodes for which ast.get_docstring is None. The exact result is saved in
[source-review evidence](verification/final_rubric_source_review.json).
All 208 normally parsed functions have docstrings, which explains why earlier
outer-module inspection did not establish this embedded-code requirement.

Consequence: the broad mandatory function-docstring criterion is not fully met
even though lint/runtime checks pass. Smallest correction: short docstrings for
these eight test wrappers, using triple-single quotes inside the outer raw
triple-double-quoted string. After approval, exercise affected CLI/bootstrap
tests and formatting/lint/type checks; update verification provenance as needed.
**The test/Python source remains unchanged for the user's review.**
This is a code-documentation gap, not a reproduced grading or persistence defect.

### CQ1 and SUB6: confirmed embedded-script lint failure

The same executable bootstrap was extracted without editing it and passed on stdin
to the existing flake8 configuration with --stdin-display-name
tests/cli_helpers_bootstrap.py. No new Python file was created. Exit 1 reports
eight E301/E302/E305 blank-line errors at embedded lines 17,26,41,76,91,103,115,124.
[Actual output](verification/final_bootstrap_lint.json) is preserved.

Consequence: all-code PEP 8 and all-lint-without-errors requirements are currently
FAIL, although saved file-level lint checks genuinely pass. Those checks parse
Python modules, not executable code inside string literals. Smallest correction:
add the required spacing/formatting in this same test bootstrap along with the
eight docstrings, then verify extracted-script lint and affected CLI/quality checks.
No lint suppression or behavior change is proposed; source edits await approval.

### CQ2 / APP1: confirmed application defect F3, fix not implemented

Location: utils/cli.py lines 233-236, the top-level KeyboardInterrupt handler.
Reproduction: inject KeyboardInterrupt at default-history lookup before the quiz,
then route the real warning printer to an OS pipe whose reader is closed.
The healthy-warning control returns 130. Both restored-diagnostic and permanently
broken-pipe variants return **1 instead of 130**; the restored variant shows a
TerminalOutputError traceback. [Exact bootstraps/stdout/stderr](verification/final_startup_interrupt_reproduction.json)
are saved. This is not a physical keyboard result.

Cause/consequence: an exception raised inside an except handler is not caught by
a sibling except clause. Expected warning-output failure can therefore override
the documented interrupt status. No completed answers exist in this pre-quiz case;
the defect is status/error handling, not demonstrated history loss.

Smallest proposed correction: catch terminal.TerminalOutputError narrowly around
terminal.warn in that KeyboardInterrupt handler and still return 130. Do not catch
unexpected programming errors. Proposed regression: healthy warning plus restored
and permanent closed-pipe cases all retain 130, show no expected-error traceback,
and create no pre-quiz history/export. **Approval required; no fix implemented.**
